Notes: Josephus, War 2.18.5 (2.477; Whiston): at the outbreak of the Great Revolt (66 CE), after Jewish rebels had raided Ptolemais among other gentile cities (2.459), the people of Ptolemais 'slew two thousand' of the Jews living among them 'and put not a few into bonds'. Earliest documented Jewish residents of Ptolemais = basis of Year Established 66 (Josephus describes them as Jews dwelling in the gentile cities). 2,000 is an ancient death toll, not a population count, so Population is blank; the resident community was at least this size if the figure is accepted (Josephus's casualty figures are treated as tendentious/possibly inflated). Earlier mentions are not Jewish residence: Ptolemais was a Phoenician-Hellenistic city hostile to the Galilean Jews (1-2 Maccabees; Simon repulsed its attacks 164 BCE; Jonathan seized there by Tryphon 143 BCE), offered by Demetrius I to the Jerusalem Temple (152 BCE) but never part of the Hasmonean or Herodian state; besieged unsuccessfully by Alexander Jannaeus c. 103 BCE; in 40 CE 'many ten thousands' of Jews came to Petronius at Ptolemais to protest Caligula's statue (Ant. 18.263) - a visiting crowd, not residents. A Christian group greeted by Paul there c. 57 CE (Acts 21:7) is assumed by some to have arisen among local Jews, but this is inference only.

Encyclopaedia Judaica ('Acre'): 'At the outbreak of the Jewish War in 66 C.E. the inhabitants massacred 2,000 of the Jewish population.' The encyclopedia thus reads Josephus's figure as Jews resident in the city (an organized community existed); 2,000 is a massacre toll, not the size of the community, so Population is blank. Josephus adds that others were imprisoned, so the community was not wholly wiped out; no source states that no Jews remained. EJ adds that the Jews 're-established their community there after the war against Rome' as the most convenient port for Galilee (undated; rabbinic period, outside this period). The city became Vespasian's base against Galilee in 67 CE and a Roman colony of veterans (under Claudius/Nero).
